title: Viasa 742
summary: Viasa Flight 742, a McDonnell Douglas DC-9-32 registered YV-C-AVD, was on the Maracaibo-to-Miami leg of a flight from Caracas when it began its takeoff roll at 12:00 on 16 March 1969. Heading toward the Ziruma district, the aircraft failed to gain altitude and its left engine struck a power pole; as the plane banked left a reflector struck the fuel tank, spilling fuel, and after hitting a second power pole the left wing was ripped off and the left engine exploded into flames before the plane crashed in La Trinidad, Maracaibo. All 84 people aboard and 71 more on the ground were killed. Investigators attributed the crash to faulty sensors along with runway and takeoff calculations made from erroneous information, which left the aircraft overloaded by more than 5,000 pounds for the prevailing conditions.
probable_cause: The cause of the crash was attributed to faulty sensors, along with runway and take-off calculations made from erroneous information, which resulted in the aircraft being overloaded by more than 5,000 pounds for the prevailing conditions.

factors.evidence: The cause of the crash was attributed to faulty sensors

events.text: The aircraft arrived at Maracaibo at 10:30; Captain Maldonado became pilot in command of the last leg and the aircraft was loaded with 12000 kg of jet fuel.
Flight 742 began its takeoff roll at 12:00, overloaded because of erroneous runway and take-off calculations.
As the DC-9 headed toward the Ziruma district it failed to gain altitude, and the plane's left engine struck a power pole.
As the plane banked left a reflector struck the fuel tank, spilling fuel; after hitting another power pole the left wing was ripped off and the left engine exploded into flames.

notes: 71 additional fatalities occurred on the ground; occupants/fatalities here reflect only those aboard the aircraft.

title: 1969 Aswan Ilyushin Il-18 crash
summary: An Ilyushin Il-18 operated by United Arab Airlines, carrying Hajj pilgrims from Jeddah to Aswan, made two unsuccessful landing attempts in darkness with visibility reduced to 2-3 kilometers by a sandstorm on 20 March 1969. On a third approach the aircraft banked right and hit the left side of the runway, tearing off the starboard wing; the resulting fuel spillage caused the wreckage to burst into flames, killing 100 of the 105 aboard. Investigators found the pilot had descended below the minimum safe altitude without the runway lights clearly in sight, and cited fatigue from continuous working hours without suitable rest as a contributory factor.
probable_cause: Pilot descended below the minimum safe altitude without having the runway lights clearly in sight. A contributory factor was fatigue arising from continuous working hours without suitable rest periods.

events.text: The flight arrived in darkness in the early morning, with visibility reduced to 2-3 kilometers due to a sandstorm, and made two unsuccessful attempts to land.
On a third approach the pilot descended below the minimum safe altitude without having the runway lights clearly in sight.
The aircraft banked to the right and hit the left side of the runway, and the starboard wing tore off.
A fuel spillage followed which caused the crashed aircraft to burst into flames.

title: Mexicana de Aviación 704

location.name: Cerro del Fraile, near El Carmen, Nuevo León

summary: Flight 704, a Boeing 727 flying from Mexico City to Monterrey, was descending toward Del Norte airport in cloudy weather with a 500-foot ceiling and haze when the crew asked whether the Ciénega de Flores beacon was operating and were told it was off from a power outage, yet reported receiving a signal resembling it. After reporting the airport in sight, the crew began final approach and struck the Cerro del Fraile mountain range, killing all 79; the last CVR minutes were missing, so investigators could not determine the cause of the deviation.

factors.evidence: the weather over the airport was cloudy with a lower boundary of 500 feet (150 m) with haze, light raining
the radio beacon at Ciénega de Flores... was not functioning... they received a signal similar to the signal from this beacon
The aircraft ended up destroyed in the Cerro del Fraile mountain range, killing all 79 people on board

events.text: The dispatcher reported the weather over the airport as cloudy with a lower boundary of 500 feet, haze and light rain.
The crew asked if the radio beacon at Ciénega de Flores was operating, and were told it was not functioning due to an electrical power outage.
Flight 704 then reported that, for some reason, they received a signal similar to the signal from this beacon.
The aircraft ended up destroyed in the Cerro del Fraile mountain range, killing all 79 people on board.

notes: Investigating board could not determine cause of deviation; last CVR minutes were missing.

title: 1969 Yukhnov mid-air collision
summary: On 23 June 1969, an Ilyushin Il-14M operating as Aeroflot Flight 831 collided in mid-air with an Antonov An-12BP of the Soviet Air Force over Yukhnovsky District. The Il-14 disobeyed ATC instructions and climbed to 3000 m to avoid turbulence, where the An-12 formation was flying. All 120 occupants of both aircraft perished.
probable_cause: The pilots of the Il-14 disobeyed instructions from air traffic control and climbed to the altitude of 3000 m to avoid turbulence and clouds, where the formation of An-12s were flying. The An-12 pilots also flew slightly lower than their assigned altitude of 3000 m, contributing to the collision.

factors.evidence: the Il-14 crew requested permission to climb to 3300 m due to severe turbulence and cumulus clouds
The pilots of the Il-14 disobeyed instructions from air traffic control and climbed to the altitude of 3000 m
The aircraft first struck at the wingtips; then the An-12's nose collided with the right horizontal stabilizer of the Il-14
The An-12 pilots were also found to be at fault for flying slightly lower than their assigned altitude of 3000 m

events.text: At 13:25 the An-12 involved in the accident took off from Kedainiai Air Base as the last one in a formation of four.
At 14:07 the Ilyushin Il-14 took off from Bykovo Airport and climbed to the assigned altitude of 2700 m.
At 14:40:55 the crew of Il-14 contacted air traffic control and requested permission to climb to 3300 m due to severe turbulence and cumulus clouds.
Due to the An-12s at 3000 m, the controller instead offered permission to descend to 2700 m, but the pilots of the Il-14 declined.
At 14:52 the two aircraft collided over Yukhnov, first striking at the wingtips, then the An-12's nose colliding with the right horizontal stabilizer of the Il-14.
The An-12 lost the right wing and right wing engines from the impact, causing it to spin to the ground, while the Il-14 lost part of the right wing and the upper part of the fuselage.

title: Nigeria Airways 925
summary: On 20 November 1969, Nigeria Airways Flight 925, a Vickers VC10 from London to Lagos with stops in Rome and Kano, crashed during final approach to Lagos International Airport. With landing gear down and flaps partially extended, the aircraft struck trees 13 kilometers short of runway 19 and crashed in thick forest. All 87 people on board were killed. The cause was not determined with certainty, but the flight recorder was not working, and investigators concluded it was most probably due to the crew being unaware of actual altitude during final approach.
probable_cause: Most probably the flight crew were unaware of the aircraft's actual altitude during the final approach and allowed the aircraft to come below safe height when not in visual contact with the ground. Fatigue may have also been a contributing factor.

title: Air France 212 (1969)
summary: Air France Flight 212, a Boeing 707 on the Caracas-to-Pointe-à-Pitre leg of a Santiago-to-Paris routing, took off from Caracas at 19:02 local time and about one minute later, at roughly 3,000 feet, plunged into the sea and sank in 160 feet of water, killing all 62 aboard. The BEA never published a report and the documents remain classified until 2029, so the cause was never established; theories include an evasive maneuver around a nearby Avro 748 followed by loss of control, a bomb, spatial disorientation, in-flight fire, engine failure and fuel contamination.

factors.evidence: maneuvers to avoid colliding with a nearby Avro 748 followed by a loss of control

events.text: The aircraft took off on the Caracas-Pointe-à-Pitre leg from runway 08R at 19:02 local time (23:02 UTC).
One minute after takeoff, at approximately 3,000 feet, the aircraft plunged into the sea and sank in 160 feet of water.
Theories about the crash have included a maneuver to avoid colliding with a nearby Avro 748 followed by loss of control, and a bomb-related explosion.

notes: BEA never published its report; cause unconfirmed among competing theories cited in the article.

title: Olympic Airways 954
summary: Olympic Airways Flight 954, a Douglas DC-6B on a domestic flight from Chania, Crete, to Athens, struck Mount Paneio near Keratea at approximately 2,000 feet with its undercarriage retracted while on approach to Athens on 8 December 1969. Rain and high winds prevailed at the time, and all 85 passengers and 5 crew aboard were killed. Investigators ruled that the flight crew had deviated from the proper track and descended below the minimum safe altitude while making an ILS approach.
